name: @jbsiddall/reactive-sqlite
//libsqlite3: Every task that touches the library needs --unstable-ffi --allow-ffi and,
critically, a DENO_SQLITE_PATH pointing at the SAME libsqlite3 the driver
loads. The driver in driver/ reads DENO_SQLITE_PATH once at import time and
otherwise falls back to the vendored build in vendor/lib/. If our FFI
dlopens a different file, the sqlite3* handle we borrow belongs to another
build and the process dies of SIGSEGV — exit 139, no message. The tasks do
not set DENO_SQLITE_PATH for you: it is host-specific, and silently guessing
it is exactly the mistake that segfaults. Export it, or let the library's
path resolution pick a system library and pass that same value to the FFI.
No task needs --allow-net: the driver never downloads a library.

tasks.check: deno fmt --check . && deno lint . && deno check

test.description: The semantic matrix: every event scenario, asserted in this process. Needs a libsqlite3 (see //libsqlite3).

test:crash.description: The crash matrix: every case runs in its OWN child process and is asserted on its exit code, so a genuine segfault (139) can never be mistaken for a pass. --allow-run is unscoped because the child is Deno.execPath(), known only at runtime; the only program spawned is this same Deno binary running test/crash_cases.ts.

table.description: Regenerate the capability x library table in README.md by probing each library, each in its own child process. --allow-run is unscoped because the child is Deno.execPath(), known only at runtime; the only program spawned is this same Deno binary running this same file in --probe mode.

test:table.description: Re-probe the three libraries and fail if README.md's capability table does not match — plus the gate that must pass before any of those numbers is reportable: three distinct files, three non-identical columns, each version found in the bytes of its own file, and one pinned known answer.

test:table-structure.description: Ask whether `Capabilities`, the table's row list and the committed README block still agree, without opening any library: every field has a row or a named exemption, every row and every exemption names a live field, the rows follow declaration order, the markers and observation date are present, and every cell is yes or no. Field names are read textually out of src/hooks.ts, because `keyof Capabilities` is the thing under suspicion. Needs no libsqlite3 and no FFI, which is why CI runs it first.

test:capability-coverage.description: Measure which capability-refusal branches are actually exercised, and by what: real absence, a simulating option, or nothing. Rewrites each refusal to `false` in the source and re-runs the semantic suite, restoring the source afterwards. --check additionally fails if the result drifts from the states recorded in the tool. --allow-run is unscoped because the child is Deno.execPath(), known only at runtime. Needs a libsqlite3 (see //libsqlite3).

test:publish.description: Assert what the published package actually contains — LICENSE and NOTICE present, test/ and tools/ absent. Spawns `deno publish --dry-run`, which validates without uploading. --allow-run is unscoped because the child is Deno.execPath(), known only at runtime.

demo.description: Run the demo in examples/: every commit-lifecycle event, the precommit veto, batching and the preupdate row values, against a real database. Not a test; needs --allow-ffi and a libsqlite3 (see //libsqlite3).

vendor:build.description: Build the vendored libsqlite3 from the pinned SQLite amalgamation into vendor/lib/<target>/. Needs a C compiler, curl and openssl; no Deno permissions are involved because the work is done by build.sh. Pass --arch aarch64 to cross-compile.

vendor:smoke.description: Compile smoke_test.c against a built library and run it, so a binary is only trusted after it has executed. Pass --arch aarch64 to run the cross-built library under qemu-user.

vendor:probe.description: Report which SQLite capabilities a libsqlite3 actually has, side by side. With no arguments it compares the prebuilt @db/sqlite downloads, the system library and the vendored build. Needs --allow-ffi.

vendor:session-demo.description: Prove the SESSION extension works in the vendored build: record a session, produce a changeset, apply it to a second database, then invert it to undo. Raw FFI, no driver. Needs --allow-ffi.
